mainTopic: What divides one domain or field from another (for שבת and for a dead גר's land), the borders of ארץ ישראל for מעשר, and עדים זוממין who testify to a חזקה.
overview: The amud opens with the end of רבי יוסי's ruling: two halves of a dried fig carried into one domain on שבת make a person חייב, but halves carried into two domains leave him פטור. רבה, אביי and רבא then argue about what splits one domain into two. רבה requires a רשות היחיד, אביי accepts even a כרמלית, and רבא accepts even a beam. רבא's view follows his rule that a domain for שבת is defined like a domain for גיטין. The גמרא then returns to acquiring a dead גר's field. Where there is no boundary, one act of acquisition covers the whole area called by the owner's name, such as 'so-and-so's well area.' A row of חצובא also divides the land, since יהושע used it to mark the borders of ארץ ישראל. This leads to teachings about borders: יהושע listed only the border towns, all land shown to משה is obligated in מעשר, and the lands of קיני, קניזי and קדמוני are excluded, with three תנאים identifying them differently. Finally a new משנה teaches that עדים זוממין who testified to a three-year חזקה pay the full value of the field. It then begins a case of three separate pairs of witnesses, one pair for each year, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: One domain makes him liable, two domains make him exempt
steps.stepSummary: The end of רבי יוסי's ruling: two halves of a dried fig carried into one domain combine and make him חייב, but halves carried into two separate domains do not combine.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he carried both halves into one domain, he is liable. If he carried them into two domains, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a quote from a ברייתא it began earlier. רבי יוסי rules on two halves of a dried fig carried out on שבת: they add up only if both landed in the same domain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The minimum amount for a חטאת on שבת is a dried fig's worth. Two half-amounts join together only if they went into one domain. If they went into two separate domains, each half stands alone, so he never reached the minimum and is פטור.

keyTerms.meaning: A domain, an area that counts as one legal space
Liable, here to bring a חטאת

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new topic starting here. It is the end of a ברייתא about שבת that the גמרא quoted just before this line, because it helps explain what divides one area from another.

phrases.english: In one domain – he is liable,
in two domains – he is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא of רבי יוסי that the גמרא brought in before this point.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two half-amounts combine for liability only when they are carried into the same domain.

steps.title: רבה: only a real private domain splits the area
steps.stepSummary: רבה says two areas count as separate only if a domain with a חטאת penalty, meaning a true רשות היחיד, stands between them. A כרמלית is not enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: This applies only when there is something between them that carries a sin-offering penalty. But a כרמלית between them does not divide them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה explains what counts as 'two domains' in רבי יוסי's ruling. Only a strong divider, a real רשות היחיד, splits the public area into two.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Carrying into or out of a רשות היחיד is a full Torah-level violation that brings a חטאת. A כרמלית is forbidden only by the רבנן, so in רבה's view it is too weak to cut one domain into two.

keyTerms.meaning: Liability to bring a sin-offering, the Torah-level penalty
An in-between area that is neither fully public nor fully private, where carrying is forbidden only by the רבנן

phrases.english: And Rabba said:
And this is only where there is a sin-offering liability between them,
phrases.notes: There has to be a real private domain sitting between the two parts of the public area.

phrases.english: but a karmelit – no.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבָּה: וְהוּא שֶׁיֵּשׁ חִיּוּב חַטָּאת בֵּינֵיהֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines what makes 'two domains' in רבי יוסי's ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only a domain carrying a חטאת penalty divides the public area. A כרמלית does not.

steps.title: אביי: even a כרמלית divides, but not a beam
steps.stepSummary: אביי makes the rule wider: a כרמלית is also enough to split the area. But a beam (פיסלא) is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Even a כרמלית divides. But a beam does not.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי disagrees with רבה and gives a more lenient line for what counts as a divider.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For אביי, what matters is that the in-between area is a separate domain in its own right, even one forbidden only by the רבנן. A plain beam lying across the way is not a domain at all, so it does not split anything.

keyTerms.meaning: A beam lying across a space

phrases.english: Abaye said: Even a karmelit,
but a beam – no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a wider view than רבה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כרמלית divides the domain. A beam does not.

steps.title: רבא: even a beam divides
steps.stepSummary: רבא goes furthest: even a simple beam is enough to make two separate domains.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Even a beam divides.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the widest view of the three. Even a small physical marker like a beam splits the area.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This connects back to our topic of fields. A beam is no weaker than a boundary (מצר) or a sea squill (חצב), and those do separate fields. So for רבא any clear physical line is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: The אמורא who holds the widest view here

steps.whyThisMatters: The three opinions form a ladder from strict to lenient: רבה needs a רשות היחיד, אביי accepts a כרמלית, and רבא accepts even a beam. Seeing this ladder makes the whole מחלוקת easy to remember.

phrases.english: Rava said: Even a beam.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even a beam divides one domain into two.

steps.title: רבא follows his own rule that שבת domains match גיטין domains
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that רבא's view fits his known rule that a domain for שבת is defined the same way as a domain for גיטין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא follows his own reasoning, as רבא said: A domain for שבת is like a domain for גיטין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that רבא's view here is not new. It matches another rule of his.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the laws of גיטין, a beam can mark off a separate domain. Since רבא says שבת domains work the same way as גיטין domains, a beam also divides for שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: He follows his own reasoning, meaning this fits a view he holds elsewhere

steps.whatToRemember: רבה needs a רשות היחיד, אביי accepts a כרמלית, and רבא accepts even a beam. רבא's view rests on his rule that רשות שבת כרשות גיטין.

phrases.english: And Rava follows his own reasoning,
as Rava said:
A domain for Shabbat is like a domain for bills of divorce.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Grounds רבא's view in a general rule he holds.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's view that a beam divides a domain
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבא's statement that a domain for שבת is like a domain for גיטין

steps.title: What if there is no boundary and no sea squill?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to acquiring a dead גר's field. It asks how far one act of acquisition reaches if nothing marks the edge of the field.
steps.simpleTranslation: If there is neither a boundary nor a sea squill there, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the side topic of שבת and returns to its main topic. It is setting up the next answer about where an acquisition stops when there are no markers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now, a מצר or חצב marked where one field ends. With no marker at all, we need another way to decide how much land one act of חזקה acquires.

keyTerms.meaning: Sea squill, a plant with deep roots used to mark field borders

phrases.aramaic: אֵין שָׁם לֹא מֶצֶר וְלֹא חָצָב,
phrases.english: If there is neither a boundary nor a sea squill there,
what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין שָׁם לֹא מֶצֶר וְלֹא חָצָב, מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the main topic of acquiring the field after the שבת side discussion.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How far one act of acquisition reaches when there is no physical border.

steps.title: רבי מרינוס: whatever is called by his name
steps.stepSummary: רבי מרינוס explains that the acquisition covers the whole area known by the owner's name.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מרינוס explained in his name: Any area that is called by his name.
steps.whatsHappening: An answer is given to the question about land with no markers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With no physical border, the border is set by what people call the place. The whole area known by one name counts as one field.

phrases.english: Rabbi Marinus explained in his name:
phrases.notes: 'His name' means רבי יוחנן, the earlier teacher whose ruling about the field is being discussed.

phrases.english: Any area that is called by his name.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The acquisition reaches the whole area that is called by the owner's name.

steps.title: What does 'called by his name' look like?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a real example of an area that is called by someone's name.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a concrete case. This sets up רב פפא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Called by his name' is a vague phrase. The גמרא wants a practical picture of it.

keyTerms.meaning: What does it look like? What is the case?

phrases.english: What are the circumstances?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for an example of the rule in step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A concrete example of an area called by someone's name.

steps.title: רב פפא: 'so-and-so's well area'
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא gives the example: land that people call 'the well area of so-and-so' all counts as one field.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Where they call it 'the place of so-and-so's well.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives the concrete example the גמרא asked for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All the land watered by one well and known by that well's name forms one unit. So one act of acquisition there covers the whole area.

keyTerms.meaning: A well, used for watering fields

steps.whatToRemember: When no boundary or sea squill marks a field, its edge is set by its common name, such as 'so-and-so's well area.'

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
Where they call it 'the place of so-and-so's well.'

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The area known as 'so-and-so's well area' counts as one field.

steps.title: A row of sea squill splits a convert's land into separate fields
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר עויא reports in the name of רבי אסי בר חנינא that a row of חצובא acts as a dividing line in the property of a dead גר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר עויא sat before רבי אסי and said in the name of רבי אסי בר חנינא: a row of חצובא divides the property of a גר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching about what counts as a dividing line in a dead גר's land. A row of חצובא plants splits it into separate fields.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 7–9 said one act of acquisition covers the whole area known by one name. This teaching adds that a row of חצובא is a real boundary. Acquiring land on one side of it does not reach the land on the other side.

keyTerms.meaning: Sea squill, a plant that was used to mark boundaries
Separates, acts as a dividing line
The property of a convert who died with no heirs, which anyone may take

phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Avya sat
before Rabbi Asi,
and he sat and was saying
in the name of Rabbi Asi bar Chanina:
phrases.notes: Two different people named רבי אסי. He is quoting רבי אסי בר חנינא while sitting in front of רבי אסי.

phrases.english: A row of sea squill serves as a divider in the property of a convert.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָתֵיב רַב אַחָא בַּר עַוְיָא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי אַסִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another way to define where one field ends in a dead גר's property, after the 'called by a name' rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A row of חצובא divides a dead גר's land into separate fields for acquisition.

steps.title: What is sea squill?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what חצובא is.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask what the word חצובא means. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling in step 10 depends on knowing what חצובא is. The גמרא wants it identified before going further.

phrases.english: What is sea squill?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the key word in the teaching of step 10.

steps.title: It is the plant יהושע used to mark the borders of the land
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of רב says חצובא is what יהושע used to set the borders of ארץ ישראל for the Jewish people.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: it is the plant with which יהושע marked out the land for ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. חצובא is the plant יהושע used to mark the borders when he divided ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This explains why חצובא counts as a divider. It was the classic boundary marker, so a row of it clearly shows where one area ends and the next begins.

keyTerms.meaning: יהושע בן נון, who divided the land among the tribes

steps.whatToRemember: A row of חצובא divides a dead גר's land into separate fields, because it is the classic boundary plant that יהושע used.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
It is that with which Joshua marked the borders of
the land for the Jewish people.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב שֶׁבּוֹ תִּיחֵם יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: חצובא is the plant יהושע used to mark the borders of ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: יהושע listed only the border towns
steps.stepSummary: Another teaching of רב יהודה in the name of רב: in his book, יהושע listed only the towns that stand on the borders.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב יהודה said in the name of רב: יהושע listed only the towns that stand on the borders.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a related teaching from the same rabbis, also about borders. The towns listed in ספר יהושע are only the ones on the borders.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a side teaching linked by topic, since step 12 was about יהושע marking borders. The towns named in ספר יהושע are there to outline each area's border, so the towns inside are not listed.

phrases.english: And Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
Joshua listed only
the towns that stand on the borders.
phrases.notes: He means the town lists in ספר יהושע. The towns deep inside each portion are not named there.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב לֹא מָנָה יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side teaching by the same rabbis on the related topic of יהושע and the borders.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The towns listed in ספר יהושע are only the border towns.

steps.title: All the land shown to משה must have מעשר taken
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of שמואל says that any area הקב"ה showed to משה is part of ארץ ישראל and its produce must have מעשר taken.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: everything that הקב"ה showed to משה is obligated in מעשר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds another teaching about the borders of ארץ ישראל. Whatever land הקב"ה showed משה before he died counts as ארץ ישראל for מעשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This sets a practical marker for where the land's מצוות apply. The view הקב"ה gave משה defines the area, and produce grown anywhere in it must have מעשר taken.

keyTerms.meaning: The Holy One, blessed be He

steps.whyThisMatters: It ties the borders of ארץ ישראל to a practical halacha: where produce must have מעשר taken.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל שֶׁהֶרְאָהוּ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְמֹשֶׁה –
phrases.english: Any area that the Holy One, Blessed be He, showed to Moses
phrases.notes: See דברים לד:א–ג, where הקב"ה shows משה the land before he dies.

phrases.english: is obligated in tithes.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל כֹּל שֶׁהֶרְאָהוּ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְמֹשֶׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the side topic of the borders of ארץ ישראל with a practical halacha.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All land הקב"ה showed משה counts as ארץ ישראל, so its produce is obligated in מעשר.

steps.title: What does שמואל's rule leave out?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which land is excluded by שמואל's rule that only land shown to משה needs מעשר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short clarifying question about שמואל's rule from the last step. If only land shown to משה counts, which land is left out?
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל gave a rule with a clear limit: the land shown to משה. A limit like that suggests some other land does not count. The גמרא wants to know exactly which land that is.

phrases.english: To exclude what?
phrases.notes: He is asking what שמואל's words 'that הקב"ה showed to משה' come to leave out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what the limit in שמואל's rule from step 14 excludes.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which land is not included in the land shown to משה, and so is free of מעשר.

steps.title: It leaves out the lands of קיני, קניזי and קדמוני
steps.stepSummary: The excluded lands are those of the קיני, קניזי and קדמוני.
steps.simpleTranslation: It excludes the קיני, the קניזי and the קדמוני.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the rule leaves out the lands of three nations: קיני, קניזי and קדמוני.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These three nations appear in the land promised to אברהם, but they were not part of what was shown to משה. So even though this land was promised, it does not yet have the status of ארץ ישראל for מעשר.
steps.confusionAlert: This land was still promised to the Jewish people. The point is only that it was not part of what was shown to משה, so the rule of מעשר does not apply there.

phrases.english: To exclude the Kenite, Kenizzite and Kadmonite.
phrases.notes: These three are named in the promise to אברהם, בראשית 15:19.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The lands of קיני, קניזי and קדמוני are excluded, so they are free of מעשר.

steps.title: Three views on which lands these nations are
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records how רבי מאיר, רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון each identify the three lands.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי מאיר says they are נפתוחא, ערבאה and שלמאה. רבי יהודה says they are הר שעיר, עמון and מואב. רבי שמעון says they are ערדיסקיס, אסיא and אספמיא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that explains which real places the three nations stand for. Three תנאים each give a different list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The old names קיני, קניזי and קדמוני are not clear on their own, so the ברייתא matches them to known places. The three תנאים disagree about which places these are. Each list has three places, one for each nation.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא
Mount Seir, the land of עשו
Ammon and Moav, the lands of the children of לוט

steps.whatToRemember: Land promised to אברהם but not shown to משה (קיני, קניזי, קדמוני) is not obligated in מעשר. The תנאים argue about which places these lands are.

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Meir says:
Naftucha, Arva'a and Shalma'a.
phrases.notes: These are names of regions. Each one matches one of the three nations, in order.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
Mount Seir, Ammon and Moav.
Rabbi Shimon says:
Ardiskis, Asya and Aspamya.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains which actual places the three nations named in step 16 refer to.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are three views. רבי מאיר says נפתוחא, ערבאה and שלמאה. רבי יהודה says הר שעיר, עמון and מואב. רבי שמעון says ערדיסקיס, אסיא and אספמיא.

steps.title: Lying witnesses about a three-year חזקה pay the full value
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה teaches that if two witnesses testify to a three-year חזקה and are found to be עדים זוממין, they pay the full value of the field.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If two witnesses testified for a man that he used a field for three years, and they were found to be זוממין, they pay him everything.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It says that witnesses who falsely tried to give someone a חזקה on a field, and were caught as עדים זוממין, must pay the full value of the field.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חזקה of three years can let the person living on a field keep it. If witnesses lie to create that חזקה, they almost made the real owner lose his field. Because of the rule of עדים זוממין, they must pay what they tried to make him lose, which is the whole field.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה; a new משנה starts here
That he 'ate' it, meaning he used the field and took its produce
Lying witnesses who were shown to have been somewhere else at the time
Holding a field for three years, which can prove ownership

steps.whyThisMatters: This connects the laws of חזקה, the topic of the פרק, with the laws of עדים זוממין. A false חזקה is treated as an attempt to take the whole field.

phrases.english: MISHNA: If two were testifying for him
that he used it for three years,
and they were found to be lying witnesses,
they pay him the whole thing.
phrases.notes: 'Him' is the real owner, the one they tried to make lose the field.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָיוּ שְׁנַיִם מְעִידִין אוֹתוֹ שֶׁאֲכָלָהּ שָׁלֹשׁ שָׁנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה, unconnected to the discussion about borders and מעשר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Witnesses who falsely testify to a full three-year חזקה and are found to be זוממין pay the owner the full value of the field.

steps.title: A new case: a different pair of witnesses for each year
steps.stepSummary: The משנה begins a case where three separate pairs of witnesses each testify about one year of the חזקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Two testified about the first year, two about the second, and two about the third —
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה sets up a new case, where each year of the חזקה has its own pair of witnesses. The ruling for this case comes in the next part of the text, so this line is only the setup.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first case, one pair of witnesses caused the whole loss. Here, each pair only testified about one year, so no single pair created the full חזקה on its own. This prepares the question of how the payment is split among the pairs.
steps.confusionAlert: The sentence is not finished here. Don't look for the ruling yet; it continues in the next part of the משנה.

phrases.english: Two in the first, two in the second,
phrases.notes: Each pair of witnesses testifies only about one year of using the field.

phrases.english: and two in the third,

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁנַיִם בָּרִאשׁוֹנָה, שְׁנַיִם בַּשְּׁנִיָּה, וּשְׁנַיִם בַּשְּׁלִישִׁית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Changes the case from step 18: instead of one pair for all three years, there are three pairs, one for each year.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Setup only: three separate pairs each testify about one year. The ruling follows in the next part of the משנה.
